title: I am building Have Words, a two player async word game
author: HokieInCH
selftext:
I've spent the past 4 months working with Claude and Claude design to build Have Words, a two player asynchronous word game.

[Perorder here](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6790067839?pt=387108&ct=Reddit&mt=8).

[TestFlight here](https://testflight.apple.com/join/R7MG8mXU).

I released a few games on the App Store about 10 years ago, kind of right around the Obj-C->Switft transition. They didn't make much money, but one was featured on every iPad in North American Apple Stores, which was really cool.

I picked up "vibe coding" last fall, and [built a game](https://winduprobotgames.com/devlog/game-i-cant-ship/) that I never got around to releasing. It's still fun to play, but it taught me everything bad about vibe coding, and where my honest-to-goodness coding skills are still required. The UX and the code were really really terrible. In fact, I think it's likely more accurate to think of the required skills as architecture. I leaned on Claude for the Swift syntax writing.

So for Have Words, I first sat down and came up with a [fundamental architecture](https://winduprobotgames.com/devlog/one-engine-four-consumers/). Not quite pen-and-paper, but no AI. Then I [came up](https://winduprobotgames.com/devlog/background-as-score/) with a [design language](https://winduprobotgames.com/devlog/ticket-wall-of-type/). Only then did I fire up Claude Design to start to put some concepts together. Waiting until then to engage AI, I believe, is what helped me avoid (I hope!) a vibe-codey, AI-sloppy looking game.

Please give the TestFlight a try, and if you're so inclined, Preorder the game on the App Store via the link above. Preorders will get the one-time IAP purchase for free, unlocking multiple color schemes and concurrent active games.

Let me know if you have any questions
